"The Coast Guard is tasked with verifying safe and secure commerce," a statement read. "It is the Captain of the Port's priority to ensure the safety of passengers, crew, the vessel, and the environment. USCG teams are verifying the cruise ship's compliance with international standards and U.S. regulations."
It was not immediately clear if the examination was initially part of a standard procedure, and what regulations may not have been met.
Its 11-night sailing that was supposed to depart from Miami on Sunday was canceled, and guests are being allowed to remain on the ship until Thursday to make travel arrangements, the cruise line said.
In a statement to NBC News, MSC said it had made the "difficult decision" to cancel the sailing.
"We recognize how disappointing and frustrating this news is for our guests, and we sincerely apologize for the disruption to their holiday," the cruise line said. "Prior to departure, a regulatory matter arose that required resolution. Despite our efforts to address the matter, we were unable to resolve it in time for the sailing to proceed. Guests will receive a full refund of their cruise fare, and we are providing support to assist with their journey home."
The MSC Poesia holds 3,223 guests and 1,039 crew members, and according to CruiseMapper, its itinerary included Jamaica, Colombia, Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras and Belize.

articles.title_orig: CrowdStrike launches AI kill switch that it says can stop internal agents that go rogue
articles.title_zh: CrowdStrike launches AI kill switch that it says can stop internal agents that go rogue
articles.content_orig:
CrowdStrike is betting that it has a solution to rogue artificial intelligence .
The cybersecurity vendor on Tuesday launched an AI kill switch designed to let security teams stop internal AI agents that go rogue, block them from relaunching and cut off their enterprise network access. The tool is built into CrowdStrike's Falcon Guardian platform, launched in September to secure AI agents. CrowdStrike also announced an integration with Anthropic's Claude Cowork .
"Having the ability to control and turn off, and make a decision and decide, I think that's really important for this next chapter of AI adoption," Chief Business Officer Daniel Bernard told CNBC.
A string of recent high-profile cyber incidents has added urgency to calls for some kind of emergency shutdown mechanism.
The Hugging Face breach orchestrated by rogue OpenAI agents in July was particularly alarming for businesses. Last week, Binance disclosed the largest crypto cyberattack on record and hackers have recently targeted hundreds of refrigerators and freezers at supermarkets in France.
Over the summer, U.S. representatives introduced bipartisan legislation that would require AI companies to build shutdown capabilities into their models.
Critics argue, however, that an emergency stop button is far too complicated to implement across multiple systems, data centers and complex AI models.
Bernard said the kill switch operates like a circuit breaker in systems where customers use its Falcon platform. The process can detect internal agent activity but requires a human to decide to cut the agent off and reinstate access.
"If you kill a process at the root, and we have that level of access at the root … it's very binary," Bernard said. "You either kill the AI and the agent, or you don't, and then you report on that."
The kill switch doesn't delete the agent's code but uses connected AI gateways to cut off access to the AI models that influence decisions, CrowdStrike said.
In the age of AI, businesses are moving quickly to adopt autonomous tools, often without the necessary safeguards and protections.
CrowdStrike believes its new tool will let companies stop AI agent 'misbehavior in its tracks, while leaving room for innovation.
The company also announced plans to acquire AI observability startup Fiddler AI and AI security testing firm Dreadnode .
CrowdStrike and its rivals are rapidly scooping up cybersecurity startups to keep up with increasing security demands. The need for AI security tools has also powered a broader wave of cybersecurity deal-making .

articles.title_orig: JetBlue Leads The Industry In Raising Checked Bag Fees… Again!
articles.title_zh: JetBlue Leads The Industry In Raising Checked Bag Fees… Again!
articles.content_orig:
For whatever reason, JetBlue tends to be the industry leader when it comes to raising checked bag fees, and competitors tend to follow. Earlier this year, JetBlue was the first major US carrier to raise checked bag fees , and now the airline is raising checked bag fees again…
Effective immediately (for tickets purchased as of November 3, 2026), JetBlue has increased checked bag fees . JetBlue has a rather complicated fee structure for checked bags, with both off-peak and peak pricing, plus different pricing based on whether you pay for the bag 24 hours or more in advance.
Below is a chart with JetBlue’s new checked bag fees.
As you can see, an off-peak first checked bag on a domestic flight will now cost you $50-60 (depending on whether you pay in advance), while a peak first checked bag on a domestic flight will now cost you $55-70 (depending on whether you pay in advance). For context, below are the dates that are considered peak for the purposes of bag fees.
It goes without saying that paying $50-70 for a first checked bag is a pretty substantial cost, especially when you consider how little checked bags used to cost. On a one-way, you’re looking at $100-140. For a family of four, you’d be looking at $400-560.
When JetBlue raised checked bag fees earlier this year, the airline released a statement claiming it was increasing checked bag fees to be “more competitive,” and that “while we recognize that fee increases are never ideal, we take careful consideration to ensure these changes are implemented only when necessary.” I imagine this time around, the logic is much of the same.
The simple reality is that oil prices are way up. Airlines have actually done a solid job of being able to make fare increases stick. But that’s not enough to fully offset the increase in the cost of jet fuel.
JetBlue is in a rough financial spot, and it hasn’t turned a profit since before the pandemic. The airline is hoping to turn an operating profit in 2027 , though that strikes me as being particularly optimistic. So the logic for raising checked bags is threefold:
JetBlue has just increased checked bag fees once again, and you’ll now pay $50-70 for a first checked bag on a domestic flight. This is JetBlue’s second price increase on checked bags so far this year. When airlines are trying to increase revenue, checked bag fees are often low hanging fruit.
When competitors match, it also becomes something that’s unavoidable for consumers, other than getting a credit card… which also has upside for the airline! I’d be shocked if other airlines don’t match this move from JetBlue.
What do you make of JetBlue increasing checked bag fees?

Shopify ( SHOP ) stock plunged 7% on Tuesday after reporting third quarter results that missed the mark on several key metrics.
The cloud-based e-commerce platform's Q3 revenue of $3.74 billion came in just shy of consensus estimates of $3.75 billion for the first time since 2022, according to Bloomberg data. articles.title_orig: Hackers behind $6.3bn Binance heist ‘used malware and bogus job interviews’
articles.title_zh: Hackers behind $6.3bn Binance heist ‘used malware and bogus job interviews’
articles.content_orig:
Firm reveals details about how its cryptocurrency exchange was compromised, saying operation began in June
The hackers behind the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) Binance heist used bogus job interviews, malicious software and an internal AI tool, the company has revealed.
The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange was compromised in an operation that began with an inadvertent download of malware in June, led to a recruitment scam in September and then a raid last week of “hot wallets” where billions of dollars worth of crypto-assets were taken.
The FBI has blamed North Korea for last week’s heist but Pyongyang, a prolific crypto-hacker , described the accusation as “absurd rhetoric” on Tuesday.
According to an update Binance released on Tuesday, the hackers got their first foothold in the summer when a company engineer inadvertently downloaded malware that exposed the employee’s role and that of others in the team that looked after Binance’s cryptowallet infrastructure.
A fake project director then contacted a different engineer on a legitimate job-hunting platform, leading to a first-round video interview with a sham HR representative and a second-round interview – on a chat app – with the “chief executive” of a fictitious company. It was during the second interview that the engineer was tricked into downloading malware on to his computer.
On 20 October, the attacker used the compromised computer plus an internal AI tool to gain control of the engineer’s system and that of a second wallet developer on the same team. Then on 29 October, the attacker used the second developer’s computer, using stolen ⁠credentials from the first engineer, and triggered a malicious script to ​launch the attack.
Binance said $2.85bn of the $6.34bn drained from cryptowallets in the attack had been frozen or intercepted.
Deepfake job interviews are a known part of North Korea’s cyber-arsenal , but normally from the other side of the process – where bogus IT professionals apply for jobs as a means of funnelling money back to Pyongyang.
“This should not have happened, and we apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry,” Binance said in the update.
The FBI said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the hack.
after newsletter promotion
But Kim Yo-jong, the influential sister of the North Korean leader Kim Jong-un , said on Tuesday that the allegations proved Washington remained hostile towards Pyongyang, according to North Korea’s state news agency, KCNA.
“The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK [the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea] as a ‘cybercriminal state,’ claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organisation ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in the incident,” KCNA quoted her as saying.
“But the US assertion ‌is absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” said Kim, a ruling party official.
“It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads international public opinion as if all the cybercrimes in different parts of the world are our deeds.”

articles.title_orig: China seeks APEC solutions to world development ahead of leaders’ summit
articles.title_zh: China seeks APEC solutions to world development ahead of leaders’ summit
articles.content_orig:
China on Tuesday urged Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) members to continue contributing practical and effective "Asia-Pacific solutions" to the region's and the world's development, according to media reports.
Top diplomat Wang Yi highlighted the importance of the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting later this month in an address to the 37th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Ministerial Meeting via video conference, state-run Xinhua News reported.
Wang, who co-chaired the meeting with Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, said Beijing is willing to work with "all parties" to do a "good job" in the final stage of the 2026 APEC "China Year" and contribute to the fruitful results at the leaders' meeting.
He said the leaders' meeting is an "important one" concerning the future development of the Asia-Pacific region.
The commerce minister urged all APEC parties to uphold free trade and innovation-driven development, foster a vibrant engine for growth, advance discussions and policy coordination on digital and intelligent economic and trade rules, and build a fair and equitable international economic and trade order.
China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China in November. It will mark the country's third time hosting the event, following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014.
The theme of the summit is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together.” China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for this year's APEC cooperation.

articles.title_orig: How To Use Your Phone To Find Hidden Cameras
articles.title_zh: How To Use Your Phone To Find Hidden Cameras
articles.content_orig:
When you feel wary, a quick check might provide some peace of mind.
For those of us who travel often, staying in a new location carries an unsettling risk: Airbnbs, hotels and other lodgings may have hidden cameras to spy on visitors. Short-term and privately owned rentals are of particular concern. While the full scale of the issue is unknown, a 2024 report from CNN found that Airbnb processed 35,000 support tickets related to "surveillance devices" in the preceding decade. While doorbell and outdoor security cameras have become increasingly common and are permitted under Airbnb rules, any indoor recording devices are banned from properties hosted on the platform.
The problem remains relatively uncommon. Airbnb said at the time of the CNN report that less than 0.1 percent of its properties were hit with safety complaints, including those related to security cameras. However, 51 percent of visitors said they don't trust short-term rentals, and such fears are not unfounded. Cameras are increasingly difficult to spot, often disguised as common home items like smoke detectors, chargers or picture frames. So it can sometimes be worth a check to ensure there are no surveillance devices in your lodging to ease your mind. But how do you find hidden cameras?
Your cell phone is a great tool to check for hidden cameras. Start with a simple flashlight sweep: close the curtains, turn off the lights, and then sweep the unit with a flashlight to check for any glimmering signs of electronics — the shine of a lens, or an LED light. Common places to hide cameras include smoke detectors, air purifiers, televisions, shower heads, or lights. Be particularly careful to check sensitive locations like near the bed or the shower. Mirrors are also important to check. If you shine a flashlight at a mirror, it should bounce back rather than passing through like a window. You can also put a finger directly onto a mirror. A real mirror will have a space between your finger and its reflection, while a two-way mirror will make it appear as though they are directly touching.
You can also use your phone camera to check for night-vision cameras in the room. These cameras emit infrared light, which on your camera app should appear as purple or white dots. To verify your phone can detect infrared light, point it at a TV remote control , push the buttons, and see if light coming from the remote can be detected. It is more likely your front-facing, or selfie camera, has this ability, but try using both to take a look. Once confirmed, you can scan the room with your phone to find IR emissions.
Many hidden cameras stream over Wi-Fi, and some mobile apps allow you to scan the network for unfamiliar devices. Options include Fing , Net Analyzer and WiFiman. Download a scanner app, connect to the Wi-Fi and search for names that you don't recognize — which will often include "cam" or "camera" to denote a recording device. Other names may map to common camera brands, like Wyze, Blink or TP-Link. Apps like Fing will show MAC addresses and device types, allowing you to further investigate names that show up in a scan. This is not always a straightforward method, however. Some devices like printers, televisions or other benign connected appliances are also likely to show up in such scans.
What's more, other devices may run their own networks, so check your phone's list of available Wi-Fi networks for similar, camera-related titles. Other cameras may use Bluetooth to connect, so a Bluetooth scan may also be helpful. To do this, you don't necessarily need a scanner app. You can just open your Bluetooth connections on the device and see what shows up.
These methods are not foolproof. Many cameras record to local memory cards, which means they won't show up on any kind of scan. Still, pairing this method with the flashlight sweep and the infrared light check is the most thorough way to check for surveillance.
If you think you have found a surveillance device in your lodging, be sure to double check using both the physical sweep method and digital scan. Once you have confirmed, do not touch the device: photograph it, reach out to the police and notify customer support for the platform you are using. Airbnb has clear policies against indoor cameras, even those that are not connected , and has in several reported cases removed hosts from the platform permanently and fully refunded guests who report such devices.
Vrbo also bans recording devices outright, and suggests guests who discover one report the incident immediately to the platform. Vrbo's policy states affected guests may be eligible for a refund. The CNN report regarding hidden cameras at Airbnb found there is no strict policy guiding employees to contact law enforcement in such incidents, so it's best to contact police yourself if you feel unsafe. Ultimately, a scan with your phone's flashlight, an infrared check with a camera and a sweep with a dedicated app can give you increased peace of mind when staying in an unfamiliar location.

articles.title_orig: What the midterm elections could mean for markets, debt
articles.title_zh: What the midterm elections could mean for markets, debt
articles.content_orig:
‘Varney & Co.’ host Stuart Varney examines a potential socialist surge, Republican upsets in red states and what an election shakeup could mean for Congress and Wall Street.
Voters across America are casting their ballots in the midterm elections on Tuesday, which will determine control of Congress and could add to investors' concerns about oversight of the artificial intelligence (AI) sector and how the debt ceiling will be addressed next year.
Since President Donald Trump's second term began in 2025 with Republican majorities in both chambers of Congress, the S&P 500 has gained about 27% in part due to a massive influx of spending on AI and strong earnings growth.
Treasury yields are also significantly higher in part because of geopolitical risks that emerged with the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, which caused a surge in energy prices. U.S. budget deficits have continued to widen to about $2 trillion, adding more upward pressure to yields as debt issuance mounts.
Investors are weighing how the results of the election will affect the outlook for financial markets depending on whether Democrats take control of one or both chambers of Congress.
AFFORDABILITY TAKES CENTER STAGE AS AMERICANS CAST THEIR BALLOTS IN HIGH-STAKES MIDTERMS
The midterm elections will determine control of Congress for the next two years, carrying implications for the nation's finances and markets. (J. David Ake/Getty Images)
Since 1930, there have been eight midterm cycles when the president's party lost control of the House, and the S&P 500 rose for the remainder of the year five times, Ned Davis Research said. It posted a median gain of 1.4% from Election Day through year-end, slightly less than the 1.9% posted across all post-Election Day midterm years.
In a scenario in which Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress , investors expect tougher oversight of AI which could weigh on markets that have been pushed higher by the emerging tech.
Democratic majorities would have the ability to investigate corporate America while attempting to slow deregulation , which could increase market volatility.
DSA PLATFORM COULD COST UP TO $212T OVER A DECADE, ANALYSIS FINDS
Markets have generally fared well under divided government. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
If Democrats win the House but Republicans hold their majority in the Senate, implications for the U.S. fiscal situation could be mixed.
Bipartisan compromises would be required over issues like funding the government to avoid shutdowns and raising the debt ceiling , which could create the potential for brinkmanship.
In a scenario where Republicans retain their majorities in the House and Senate, the GOP could pursue further tax reforms or boost defense spending.
FEDERAL BUDGET DEFICIT HITS $2T AS NATIONAL DEBT COSTS SURGE
The results of the midterms will impact negotiations between Congress and the Trump administration depending on who controls the House and Senate. (Grant Baldwin/AFP via Getty Images)
Ned Davis chief U.S. strategist Ed Clissold said that a House takeover by Democrats could modestly temper the U.S. equity market's year-end rally, but in general it hasn't prevented stocks from advancing.
"Conventional wisdom is that gridlock is good (for stocks)," said Clissold, adding that stocks have performed better under Democratic presidents than Republicans.
Diego Barnuevo, market analyst at Ebury, said that a Democratic-held Congress' negotiations with the White House would likely be limited to the budget and debt ceiling, and that a "Democratic sweep would be neutral to mildly positive for the fiscal outlook."

A Republican sweep could ease concerns over investigations into AI companies that carry the potential to rattle markets.
"If Republicans maintain control of Congress, that would likely provide the most supportive incremental federal policy backdrop for the AI/infrastructure buildout through policy continuity, potential fiscal expansion, deregulation and faster federal permitting," JPMorgan strategists said in a note.
Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: US billionaire Todd Boehly’s consortium buys frozen Lukoil securities at 70% discount, moving closer to $22 billion asset deal spanning oil and gas interests in five African countries
articles.title_zh: US billionaire Todd Boehly’s consortium buys frozen Lukoil securities at 70% discount, moving closer to $22 billion asset deal spanning oil and gas interests in five African countries
articles.content_orig:
A consortium led by US billionaire Todd Boehly has moved closer to acquiring a global portfolio of Lukoil assets that includes oil and gas interests across five African countries.
A bank acting for the consortium has reportedly bought billions of dollars of frozen Lukoil securities from Western investment funds, positioning the group for a proposed exchange of the securities for the Russian oil company’s international assets.
The portfolio was initially valued at about $22 billion, although its value has since declined after sanctions disrupted some operations. The figure covers Lukoil’s entire international portfolio across Africa, Europe, the Middle East and other markets, not its African assets alone.
If completed, the transaction could shift Lukoil’s interests in Egypt, Cameroon, Ghana, Nigeria and the Republic of Congo into an investment structure backed by American and Gulf investors.
The consortium includes Boehly, Emirati investment groups International Holding Company and Al Hail Holding, the Syrian-Qatari Al-Khayat brothers and the US International Development Finance Corporation, the American government’s overseas investment agency.
According to Reuters⁠, a bank representing the consortium acquired the frozen securities from about 10 US and British investment funds, as well as American depositary banks that held them for retail investors. The securities were reportedly bought at about 30 cents on the dollar.
The transaction has not been completed, and representatives of Boehly, Lukoil and the US development agency did not confirm the proposal to Reuters. However, people familiar with the process said an agreement could be reached within weeks.
Forbes estimates Boehly’s fortune at about $9.2 billion. The American investor co-founded Eldridge Industries and holds interests across insurance, finance, media and sport, including stakes in the Los Angeles Dodgers and Los Angeles Lakers. He also led the group that acquired Chelsea Football Club in 2022.
Lukoil’s African holdings include producing assets, undeveloped discoveries and deepwater exploration projects involving several national oil companies and international energy groups.
In Egypt, Lukoil holds 50% interests in the West Esh El-Mallaha oilfield and its extension. It also owns 24% of the Meleiha concession, where Italian energy company Eni controls the remaining 76%.
In Cameroon, the Russian company holds 30% of the Etinde offshore block. The 460-square-kilometre project is located in the Gulf of Guinea, close to the country’s maritime border with Equatorial Guinea.
Lukoil also owns 18% of Nigeria’s offshore OML 140 block, where Chevron is the operator. The block covers more than 1,200 square kilometres and includes the Nsiko discovery and other prospective structures.
In the Republic of Congo, Lukoil owns 25% of the Eni-operated Marine XII project. The block contains the producing Nene oilfield and Litchendjili gas-condensate field and supplies gas to Congo’s expanding liquefied natural gas operations.
The company paid $800 million for its Marine XII interest in 2019, providing one of the few publicly disclosed valuations for an individual African asset within the wider portfolio.
Ghana represents one of the most commercially and politically sensitive parts of any proposed transaction.
Lukoil holds 38% of the Deepwater Tano Cape Three Points block, which contains the undeveloped Pecan oilfield. Pecan Energies, owned by the Africa Finance Corporation , operates the block with a 50% interest, while the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation holds 10% and Fueltrade owns the remaining 2%.
Ghana was reported in May to be considering the use of pre-emptive rights to acquire Lukoil’s interest. Such rights could give existing partners or the government priority over an outside buyer and mean that not every African asset automatically transfers to Boehly’s consortium.
Lukoil began looking for buyers for its overseas assets after the United States imposed sanctions on the company in October 2025 as part of efforts to reduce Russia’s oil revenue.
American private equity company Carlyle previously agreed to pursue the portfolio but later withdrew from the process, leaving Boehly’s consortium as the leading bidder.
The Boehly proposal is structured as a cashless transaction. Frozen Lukoil securities acquired from Western investors would be exchanged for the company’s international assets, while the securities intended for Lukoil would reportedly be placed in an escrow account.
That structure is designed to prevent Lukoil from receiving immediate financial benefit from the sale. It also allows Western investors to recover part of the value of securities that have been frozen or written down since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine .
However, the transaction still faces a significant regulatory question.
The US Treasury ’s Office of Foreign Assets Control⁠ says its current licence permits negotiations, due diligence and contingent contracts but does not authorise the actual transfer of Lukoil’s assets.
Treasury guidance also says an approved transaction must sever the international business from Lukoil, keep any money owed to the Russian company blocked under US jurisdiction and avoid providing it with an upfront windfall, including through an asset or share swap.
The negotiating licence expires on 21 November 2026. Boehly’s consortium would therefore require separate US Treasury approval before taking control of any African or other international assets.
A successful transaction would give the US-backed consortium interests alongside companies including Chevron, Eni and African national oil groups. It would also mark a significant change in the ownership of energy resources across five African markets.
For Lukoil, the proposed sale would mean surrendering international assets while being prevented from immediately accessing much of their value. For Western investors, it offers an exit from frozen securities, but at a reported discount of about 70%.
African governments and existing project partners, meanwhile, will determine whether individual assets can be transferred and whether they prefer the proposed new investors, domestic ownership or alternative buyers.

articles.title_orig: Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI
articles.title_zh: Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI
articles.content_orig:
Google announced Tuesday morning that it would switch off AI products by default for students in schools that use the technology giant’s education software. But those schools that forgo its AI services would also be cut off from Google Search.
The move comes after mounting criticism from advocacy groups and senators about the spread of Google’s AI services available in classrooms. Until Tuesday, its AI products — branded under the Gemini moniker — were automatically activated for schools using Google Classroom.
Google said Tuesday’s move would also cut off students’ access to Google Search if schools do not enable Gemini, given AI’s growing integration into the company’s search products.
Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education, said in a blog post announcing the change that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search “will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.”
“We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach,” Phillips wrote.
Some education and technology advocates immediately slammed the decision, painting the move as a punishment for schools that don’t use Google’s AI. “It is unfortunate that Google has prioritized its business interests over the education of our children,” said Randi Weingarten, president of the American Federation of Teachers, a national educators union.
“Instead of working with teachers and parents to uphold privacy and ensure their tools are safe and useful, it throws the baby out with the bathwater and bans access to the tools altogether,” she told NBC News in written comments.
Josh Golin, executive director of advocacy group Fairplay, said in a statement that Google is attempting “to strong-arm schools into using its AI products.”
“Schools should use this opportunity to help students find more privacy-protective alternatives for search, as well as ways to do more substantive research beyond search and click,” Golin said.
In a statement posted to social media after this article was published, Google said the announcements “give schools more choice, not less,” and that schools can turn on Google Search individually without enabling Gemini products. But Search will still have AI features built into it, which the company said have been updated “to make it better for learning. Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.”
Earlier this year, Google turned on Gemini in its Classroom app, allowing children — regardless of age — to access AI products unless districts disabled it .
Parent advocacy groups and experts on the use of technology in schools denounced Google for providing AI products to children — raising concern that students would outsource their work to AI systems on school devices — and lobbied school districts to disable Gemini products. In an open letter in early October, 13 leading parent advocacy organizations — including the Digital Childhood Institute and Schools Beyond Screens — called on school districts to turn off access to Gemini and YouTube, which is also owned by Google .
Google has established a dominant role in education technology over the past 15 years. The vast majority of Chromebook laptops are purchased by school districts to provide to students. Nearly two-thirds of assignments use a Google product, according to a 2023 report by the firm Schoolytics. This year, the company began offering multiday AI trainings for educators, featuring sessions that focused on how they could mitigate pushback by teachers who don’t want to use AI.
Research on AI in educational settings has not established a long-term benefit for students. There are no high-quality causal studies into student use of AI, according to the SCALE Initiative at the Stanford Graduate School of Education . Researchers have also warned that many of the studies conducted so far on AI in education didn’t measure whether it boosted learning and often did not test whether AI-assisted learning was superior to other teaching methods.
In Tuesday’s blog post , Google said that for schools that enable the company’s AI products, they will now detect when a student is trying to use them just to get an answer on an assignment. A redesigned version of Google Search will instead walk students through the topic or problem and work through the concepts, without going directly to the answer, the company said.
Jared Perlo is a technology reporter focused on AI for NBC News Digital.
Tyler Kingkade is a national reporter for NBC News, based in Los Angeles.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
articles.title_zh: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
articles.content_orig:
ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.
ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.
In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.
Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)
Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree. (OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in-house search index, although there is still some speculation that it routes some queries through Google.)
The news comes amid an ongoing search engine shake-up, as Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third-party sites and invests heavily in AI tools — not just AI Overview but also additional generative AI capabilities , including personalized search results with visualizations and charts. But as search queries increasingly route through OpenAI and other AI labs’ services, other companies are investing in the same types of AI-focused search experience, even if they call it something else: for OpenAI, it’s “Intelligent UI,” or creating a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response. “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” Fry said.
Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year. OpenAI has defended its ads in the past, and Fry told reporters they hadn’t produced a lasting backlash. “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” he said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.”
OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before.
“Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.

articles.title_orig: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
articles.title_zh: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
articles.content_orig:
The New York Times and other newspaper companies sued Brave Software yesterday, alleging that the browser maker illegally bypasses paywalls and sells stolen news content to AI companies.
“Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere,” the NYT alleged in a lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Citing third-party revenue estimates, the suit claimed that “Brave has made more than $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work without consent or permission,” while “publishers have received nothing.”
The lawsuit said, “AI companies pay Brave to provide them with real-time online content from the Brave search index,” and use content from the Brave index “to train their own AI models” and “to respond to specific user queries.” The NYT lawsuit points to Brave’s website , which says the Brave Search API is “used by some of the biggest names in AI, including Cohere, Mistral, Perplexity, and You.com.”
The lawsuit accused Brave of all the major types of copyright infringement: direct infringement, contributory infringement, and vicarious infringement. The lawsuit claims Brave infringes copyrights directly by scraping articles for its search index, for its “Ask Brave” AI search feature, and for the Brave API that “serves as an illicit source of unlicensed copyrighted material, including Times journalism, to other AI companies.”
The NYT accused Brave of being “a contributory and vicarious infringer when it deliberately induces, facilitates, controls, and profits from its users’ and GenAI customers’ copying of the copyrighted content.” Finally, the lawsuit said Brave violated the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) by circumventing technological measures the NYT and other content owners use to restrict access to their articles.
“The Brave Browser includes a default setting that, when activated, causes the browser to go behind website paywalls and provide the paywalled content to the user,” the lawsuit said. The browser “blocks advertising that would otherwise appear on The Times’s website, and instead shows its own ads, offering its users a cut of the revenue even as it deprives The Times of digital advertising revenue that helps it fund the expensive effort of producing journalism,” the lawsuit said.
When testing the Brave browser for Mac today, we found that the optional “paywall blocker” feature made it possible to read a paywalled New York Times article. The feature was enabled in the default settings and can be turned off.
The NYT asked for a permanent injunction to stop Brave from continuing the allegedly illegal conduct. The lawsuit seeks statutory damages, actual damages, restitution of profits derived from alleged copyright infringement, and “restitution and disgorgement of all revenue and profits Brave obtained through its ad-substitution scheme.”
A similar lawsuit was filed against Brave in the same court yesterday by the New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune, and Orlando Sentinel companies. We contacted Brave and will update this article if it provides a response.
Perplexity, which is not a defendant in the Brave lawsuit but is facing a different lawsuit filed by the NYT, accused the news organization of “disinformation” in a statement provided to Ars and other news outlets. Perplexity’s statement did not identify any specific inaccuracies in the lawsuit against Brave.
“The New York Times is overpaying its attorneys and underpaying its journalists. (Who could’ve easily identified the disinformation in this suit.),” Perplexity’s statement said.
The NYT sued Perplexity in December 2025, alleging that its AI tool gives users “outputs that are identical or substantially similar to” NYT articles, including “verbatim or near-verbatim reproductions, summaries, or abridgements of the original content.” Perplexity’s response to that lawsuit said its answer engine only fetches content from copyrighted articles in reply to user queries. Perplexity argued that “developing an AI tool that can allegedly automatically fetch and provide specific content in response to user requests based on its pre-configuration and access to materials available on the Internet” is not “volitional conduct.”
The NYT also sued OpenAI and Microsoft in December 2023 in a lawsuit alleging that OpenAI trains its AI with stolen news content. The lawsuit is heading toward a trial , with OpenAI arguing that its use of news articles is fair use under copyright law.

articles.title_orig: US Stocks Waver as Election, AI Bubble Risks Weigh on Outlook
articles.title_zh: US Stocks Waver as Election, AI Bubble Risks Weigh on Outlook
articles.content_orig:
Buckle up for another wild week in markets.
Investors are still coming off a roller coaster ride that included a painful sell-off in the AI trade on Friday, but the volatility isn't expected to die down soon, and a handful of potential catalysts is lies ahead for investors.
This week's docket includes more Big Tech earnings , economic data updates, and the midterm elections, which have historically been a hurdle for markets to clear.
And then there's the fragile state of the AI trade, which was rattled last week as concerns about capex and overall AI demand rocked the market. The Nasdaq 100 , which logged its worst month in over a year, is now on the edge of entering an official correction, with the tech-heavy index down 9% from its high in early October.
Here's what investors are facing next:
Apple , the largest company in the world by market cap after Nvidia's plunge last Friday, is on deck to report results for the third quarter after the bell on Monday, a marquee event that's expected to shape sentiment in the tech trade after last week's sell-off. Here's what Wall Street is expecting from the iPhone maker:
Investors will be paying special attention to the firm's comments on AI. Apple isn't a capex story the same way companies like Meta and Microsoft are. Its spending is expected to come in at around $11 billion to $14 billion this year, compared to the $100+ billion from AI hyperscalers, but the market remains eager to see what the iPhone maker's AI ambitions will look like in the post-Tim Cook era. The coming earnings call will be the first to be led by new CEO John Ternus , setting the tone for the tech giant's new chapter.
The market has been mercurial on Big Tech earnings lately, with investors ready to punish big AI firms at any whiff of bad news. Meta and Tesla were negatively impacted after reporting third-quarter results that hinted at slight changes in spending outlooks, triggering fears that slowing investment could spark a wave of knock-on effects for other suppliers in the industry.
Amazon and Alphabet, on the other hand, spooked investors by suggesting capex would grow next year despite negative cash flow, leading the market to punish those tech giants for what it saw as excessive spending.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Palantir , another notable player in the AI universe, will also report earnings after the bell.
"We continue to evaluate the monetization versus spending conundrum for hyperscalers," Eric Freedman, the CIO at Northern Trust, wrote in a note on Monday. "While results were very company-specific, the common threads markets focus on are capital expenditure plans, financing needs, existing business cannibalization and evidence of returns."
Oil is an enduring story in markets in 2026, one that's sparked major bouts of volatility in both stocks and bonds. On Monday, Brent and West Texas Intermediate crude eacg dropped 6% as investors took in the possibility that the US and Iran could revive attempts at a diplomatic resolution to the war.
State Secretary Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump preferred to wrap up the conflict with Iran "peacefully," adding that the president hasn't yet decided to attack Iran.
However, more volatility could be looming.
Oil prices spiked in recent weeks on a New York Times report that the US and Israel are drawing up plans to strike Iran after the midterm elections. Energy markets could see more volatility this week if the market sees fresh signs evidence that peace talks are progressing or the administration signals that strikes will resume.
After months of anticipation, the midterm elections are finally here.
Wall Street is eyeing the passing of the midterm elections as a potential catalyst for markets. Stocks have historically struggled into the midterms, but have seen strong gains in the months following, with the S&P 500 gaining an average of 14% in the six months after the midterms since 1970, according to an analysis from BlackRock.
JPMorgan Private Bank said it was eyeing "outsized" gains in the S&P 500 , pointing to improved market breadth, or the measure of winning stocks to losing stocks, in the overall index lately. The bank also recently lifted its year-end price target for the S&P 500 to 8,000, implying 4% upside from the index's current levels.
The bank's market intelligence team flagged near-term volatility depending on the results of the election and outlined the possible reaction in stocks depending on each election outcome.
S&P 500 drops as much as 25 basis points or gains as much as 50 basis points.
Some investors fear an "AI sell-off" in the event of a Democratic sweep, but in that scenario, any pullback in markets would be an "opportunity to buy the dip," strategists wrote in a note.
"SPX has been up a year after every midterm election since 1950 with an average gain of around 15%," the bank's Craig Cohen wrote in a client note. "I suspect that at least part of the reason for this tendency is that the midterms tend to see the incumbent party loses seats and gridlock in Washington tends to be good for Wall Street."
" Volatility could stay up awaiting results. Typically, stocks rally after midterms, but one exception was 2018—also a rate hike year," Joe Mazzola, a head trading and derivatives strategist at Charles Schwab, wrote in a note.
Finally, investors will get a major macroeconomic update in the October jobs report on Friday. It's a data point that could shape the Fed's projected path for interest rate hikes through the rest of this year and early next year.
Central bankers left rates unchanged at their last policy meeting , as expected, pointing to the need to assess the trajectory of inflation before moving rates further. Markets, though, are expecting a rate hike at the Fed's next policy meeting, with the probability of a 25 basis-point rate increase rising to 78% on Monday, according to CME FedWatch.
A strong jobs report, while good news for the economy, risks creating a reason for investors to sell stocks. The logic is that a stronger job market reflects the economy's capacity to absorb higher interest rates, a possible drag for risk assets.
Economists are expecting the US to have added 55,000 payrolls last month, up from the 29,000 jobs added in September.

articles.title_orig: Germany’s Merz warns Europe needs seat at the table as Trump renews Ukraine talks
articles.title_zh: Germany’s Merz warns Europe needs seat at the table as Trump renews Ukraine talks
articles.content_orig:
Speaking alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Berlin on Tuesday, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he had seen no sign that Russia is serious about negotiating a ceasefire in Ukraine.
Zelenskyy and Merz both said the European Union must help shape any lasting peace.
Germany expects European representatives to be in Abu Dhabi for next week's US-led talks with Ukraine and Russia , though they are unlikely to have a seat at the table.
"It is important that Russia finally and seriously engages in negotiations about a ceasefire and a subsequent peace agreement," Merz said when asked about the Abu Dhabi talks. "I do not see that happening so far."
Zelenskyy said he hopes the Abu Dhabi talks, the first trilateral sit down since February, could pave the way for a direct meeting between the Ukrainian president and Russia's Vladimir Putin, who has thus far refused several offers from Zelenskyy for face-to-face talks.
"We are counting on the fact that work in this format and our other diplomatic steps will open the way to a trilateral format at the level of leaders," he told reporters.
Merz said Europe must have a say on sanctions and postwar security.
He said the local ceasefire in Oleshky could serve as a model for a wider truce, but warned that Russian attacks in the Black Sea risked further escalation. "Russia is precipitating a global food crisis, to the detriment of the poorest nations and countries in the world," he said.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine wanted a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, safe passage for grain shipments through the Black Sea and further prisoner exchanges.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
The Ukrainian president said a ceasefire alone would not secure a lasting peace. Ukraine would need security guarantees backed by Europe and the US. He insisted Europe must be involved in the negotiations.
"There cannot be a sustainable peace if Europe is not at the negotiating table," Zelenskyy said.
He said Ukraine would join the US, European partners and NATO for talks on security guarantees and reconstruction in Brussels on Wednesday.
The talks in Berlin come as Russia continues to increase airstrikes on Ukrainian civilians.
Zelenskyy said at least 33 people were killed, and more than 50 could be trapped in rubble, after multiple Russian strikes on a school building used as an aid distribution center in the frontline southeastern village of on Monday.
Ukrainian officials said Russian forces launched an initial strike on residents waiting to receive aid, and then hit the same location again after waiting for rescue personnel to arrive on the scene, killing several of them and destroying emergency vehicles.
Speaking in Berlin, Zelenskyy described the strike as "one of the largest Russian killings of this war."
On Tuesday, at least 73 people were injured in a strike on a hospital in the northeastern city of Kharkiv, and 226 patients had to be transferred to other hospitals, regional prosecutors said.
"Ahead of the next winter, air defense and the energy sector are our priorities," Merz said. He said Germany would soon deliver new aid in both areas and provide further winter assistance this year.
Zelenskyy thanked Germany for helping protect Ukraine's skies and supporting its energy infrastructure.
"Without Germany, we would not be as strong as we are," he said.
He said Ukraine urgently needed more air defense equipment, including Patriot interceptors .
Zelenskyy told EU leaders in October that Ukraine would need an additional €70 billion ($78 billion) from European governments next year. Germany plans to host a summit of countries backing Ukraine in mid-November to discuss further support ahead of winter.
The visit coincides with the opening of the two-day Berlin Security Conference, which brings together European officials and defense experts. Russia's war in Ukraine is high on the agenda.
Police said about 3,400 additional officers were deployed for the visit and the conference, with reinforcements from across Germany.
Armed officers guarded barriers around parts of the government district, and special police units deployed snipers. Roads were also closed in western Berlin, including near the Kurfürstendamm shopping avenue.

articles.title_orig: China’s HQ-9B air defense system destroys maneuvering missile in tests
articles.title_zh: China’s HQ-9B air defense system destroys maneuvering missile in tests
articles.content_orig:
Authorities in Beijing announced that the PLA Air Force utilized the HQ-9B surface-to-air missile platform to successfully neutralize targets during a training drill. These objectives consisted of missiles capable of rapid movement and complex maneuvering.
The evaluations of the HQ-9B, a modern addition to the Chinese military inventory, required the interception of two distinct missile varieties. One specific target executed an abrupt mid-air pivot before plummeting toward the earth at extreme velocity.
According to the state media outlet China Central Television (CCTV), the Central Theater Command's Shenwei Missile Battalion within the PLA Air Force carried out the maneuvers.
Personnel from the Shenwei Missile Battalion were not briefed on the specific nature of the incoming threats; they were informed only that the mission involved engaging agile, high-velocity projectiles.
A battalion participant noted that the crew was afforded a mere two-second window to react. In this brief interval, they were required to identify the mysterious object and determine if a launch was necessary.
Military specialist Song Zhongping remarked, in a report by the Global Times , that despite precise radar monitoring, a defense system must possess the capacity for mid-flight trajectory adjustments to successfully follow a target exhibiting erratic flight patterns.
For guidance and tracking during an engagement, the HQ-9B utilizes an active radar homing (ARH) mechanism paired with an inertial navigation system (INS). Beyond its sophisticated steering and engine technologies, the HQ-9B is capable of striking targets that follow non-linear flight paths. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of a missile intercept is contingent upon multiple variables, such as communication reliability, target velocity, reaction speed, and radar precision.
The drill also showcased the PLA's ability to fuse different missile, command, and radar elements into a cohesive air defense web. Expert Song Zhongping clarified that China has established a unified data-sharing architecture for its diverse air defense branches to distribute intelligence on approaching hazards and synchronize their actions. Threats are distributed among various units depending on their proximity and combat readiness.
Hu Yang, another member of the battalion, mentioned that just two minutes elapse between the reception of a high-level warning and the actual interception. While the drill proves the HQ-9B can hit maneuvering missiles, its capacity to stop hypersonic cruise missiles or glide vehicles requires separate validation through authentic combat simulations.
Although the HQ-9B might intercept a target approaching directly, engaging hypersonic cruise missiles or glide vehicles presents an extreme challenge for any surface-to-air hardware. Testing the HQ-9B against maneuvering aerial targets does not verify its effectiveness against operational hypersonic technology. Assessing the system's utility against such weaponry would require distinct trials in practical operational settings.
Earlier, during September 2025, China exhibited numerous air defense assets . Featured hardware included the HQ-29, HQ-19, HQ-9C, and HQ-9B. These platforms represent China's expanding proficiency in defending against diverse missile types and fixed-wing aircraft.
The latest HQ-9B drills highlight the ongoing technical advancement of China's armed forces. Still, the ability of the system to negate sophisticated missile hazards remains unproven until subjected to independent testing in lifelike combat scenarios.

articles.title_orig: Poland Beefs Up Security at Border With Russia
articles.title_zh: Poland Beefs Up Security at Border With Russia
articles.content_orig:
Polish authorities deployed additional police, counterterrorism units, and border guards to the country’s frontier with Russia’s Kaliningrad region after intelligence warned of possible sabotage or an armed provocation, RMF24 reported on November 3.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that Polish and allied services had warned that acts of sabotage or more serious provocations could occur along the border with Russia in early November.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Poland had already launched a special security operation along the Kaliningrad border on November 2 after Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible armed incursions and sabotage.
“After receiving more precise information that incidents could occur in the first half of November, including armed people entering Polish territory, we decided to send substantial police forces, counterterrorism units, and reinforce the Border Guard,” Tusk stated .
He added that shortly after midnight, the Border Guard reported “disturbing movement” along the Polish-Russian border involving “individuals with flashlights.”
“We very quickly mobilized the appropriate forces and resources there, and managed to prevent a provocation,” Tusk stated.
According to RMF24, Polish services intervened near Sępopol in the Warmian-Masurian region. No one crossed into Polish territory, and the observed individuals withdrew deeper into the Kaliningrad region.
Tusk noted that the incident did not result in any serious consequences but warned that Russian pressure could continue.
“It is not the case that we avoided some tragic events tonight, but we must remain very focused,” he stated. “Tension and escalation from Russia may continue, and we still need to remain focused and ready to prevent possible provocations.”
Polish police have established a special operations headquarters covering the Warmian-Masurian and Podlaskie regions, with the Border Guard also participating.
Russia has also escalated rhetoric around Kaliningrad in recent months. In September, the Russian Embassy in the UK warned that any NATO attack or blockade of the exclave could trigger a response “using all means available to Russia, including nuclear weapons.”

articles.title_orig: Israeli ex-generals condemn settler violence, help Palestinian farmers
articles.title_zh: Israeli ex-generals condemn settler violence, help Palestinian farmers
articles.content_orig:
A group of senior Israeli ex-military officials helped Palestinian farmers on Tuesday to harvest olives , in a gesture of solidarity amid an upsurge in extremist settler violence targeting Palestinians in the West Bank.
"When I see what is going on here, when I see these guys come... and hit women and kids, it reminds me of stories from my parents from the time when the Jewish people suffered," said Maj.-Gen. (ret.) Eyal Ben-Reuven, who compared the extremist settler attacks to pogroms.
Ben-Reuven said he began organizing a group of around 30 senior military officials, including six generals, several months ago following an increase in extremist settler violence.
The IDF has said it condemns violence and it operates to maintain security in the West Bank .
"Occupation is the main problem of Israeli society. I believe we must deal with it, we cannot ignore it. We must try to solve it together with the Palestinians," said Col. (ret.) Doron Meinert.
Ben-Reuven and others said they were also concerned about the impact of settler violence on Israel's global reputation.
"Strategically, tactically, it's creating problems for the state of Israel in the West and the United States," said Jonatan Yoni, a former brigadier-general, who said he was also motivated by the plight of Palestinian farmers and by opposition to Israeli annexation of the West Bank.
Meinert, who now dedicates much of his time to volunteering in the West Bank in support of Palestinians, also said that the IDF aided the settlers.
Some Israeli soldiers, Meinert added, share the extremist settlers' belief that only Jews "have the right to this area and that the Arabs should be expelled or stay here as second (class) residents."
The IDF has said it is the people's army and reflects the full spectrum of views in Israeli society.

articles.title_orig: Israeli Claims of Iranian Chemical Weapons Divide U.S. Officials
articles.title_zh: Israeli Claims of Iranian Chemical Weapons Divide U.S. Officials
articles.content_orig:
Israel has provided the United States with intelligence indicating that Iran is considering using chemical weapons against its adversaries, but officials in Washington are divided over the information's credibility and significance, The New York Times reported on Tuesday, citing American and regional officials.
Some senior US officials received the intelligence with concern, while others expressed deep skepticism, viewing it as part of a pressure campaign by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government aimed at convincing the Trump administration to resume large-scale fighting against Iran .
According to the report, during discussions with US intelligence agencies and other officials over the past two weeks, senior Israeli officials presented the chemical weapons threat as more urgent than Iran's ambitions to develop nuclear weapons.
Israeli intelligence officials told their American counterparts that they believe Iran is rapidly advancing technology that would allow it to mount chemical weapons on missiles or smuggle them into Israel or another country to carry out an attack.
Other senior American officials believe the threat should be taken seriously, particularly in light of a series of recent warnings about Iranian preparations to attack US interests.
According to the newspaper, there is little disagreement within the American intelligence community that Iran is developing chemical weapons. The central dispute concerns whether Iranian leaders would actually use them, particularly if Iran is not attacked again.
Israel also shared some of the intelligence with officials in Gulf states. Several questioned whether Iran was developing plans to use chemical weapons and believe Israel is attempting to push the United States and its partners toward a more intensive phase of the war.
A regional official told the newspaper that Israel had presented Gulf countries with assessments suggesting Iran was working to make its chemical weapons operational, but had not shared supporting evidence.
According to the official, Gulf governments regarded the claims as lacking seriousness.
For some American officials, the warnings have revived memories of the faulty intelligence surrounding Iraq's weapons of mass destruction in 2002.
At the time, US intelligence agencies presented the White House with a firm assessment that Iraq possessed such weapons, although the country had largely abandoned or suspended its nuclear, chemical and biological weapons programs.
Even among those briefed on the new intelligence, assessments differ regarding how quickly and effectively Iran could deploy chemical weapons.
According to experts and American officials who spoke with the newspaper, mounting a chemical weapon on a ballistic missile is not particularly difficult, but ensuring the effective dispersal of the chemical agent is more complicated.
Smuggling a bomb across a border also presents difficulties. Another possibility mentioned was the use of a drone.
Despite the Israeli warnings, the newspaper reported that preparations for responding to chemical weapons attacks are not a central component of the Home Front Command exercises taking place across Israel this week.
Two Home Front Command officials said there had also been no widespread reminders distributed to officers or the public regarding protective instructions against such a threat.
The IDF declined to comment.
The intelligence was shared as the United States and Iran explore the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough while simultaneously preparing for a resumption of hostilities.
According to senior American officials, US Central Command (CENTCOM) has a plan for an attack on Iran that could be carried out as early as Wednesday, November 4, one day after the US midterm elections.
The report stated that three American aircraft carriers are currently in the region, while the preferred operational window for an attack is expected to be brief.
One of the aircraft carriers will need to return to its home port after the beginning of November, and particularly dark nights are expected in the coming days, providing favorable conditions for military operations.
However, President Donald Trump has not yet approved a large-scale attack, and diplomatic contacts between Washington and Tehran are continuing.
In recent weeks, the United States has concentrated warships, fighter jets and bombers in the region in preparation for a possible relatively short military campaign involving intensive strikes.
At the same time, diplomats are attempting to formulate an agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, address Iran's nuclear program and postpone further military action.
According to the report, the military buildup could also serve as leverage to support the diplomatic effort.
Meanwhile, US intelligence agencies assess that the threat to Americans in the Middle East and several other countries is at its highest level since the war began in February.
Intelligence collection was intensified after an Iranian plot to attack a base in Britain used by American fighter jets was uncovered.
On October 23, a warning memorandum regarding potential Iranian attacks was sent to senior administration officials. Diplomats and other personnel were subsequently placed on heightened alert.
The newspaper also linked Netanyahu's efforts to his political situation following the Israeli elections, in which he failed to secure a clear path toward forming a government.
Several commentators who spoke with the newspaper suggested that Netanyahu might attempt to use a national security emergency to pressure opposition leaders into joining a coalition under his leadership.
American allegations regarding an Iranian chemical weapons program date back decades.
In 2003, Iran acknowledged that it had developed chemical capabilities during the Iran-Iraq War but claimed that it subsequently dismantled them.
Tehran denies possessing chemical weapons and has previously described such accusations as psychological warfare conducted by Israel and Netanyahu .
Dana Stroul, a former senior Pentagon official responsible for Middle East policy during the Biden administration, said it has been known for more than two decades that Iran has been stockpiling components for chemical weapons, but has never used them.
However, she warned that Tehran could feel "existential pressure" and potentially cross the threshold into directly using such weapons offensively.
A spokesperson for Netanyahu's office told the NYT : "Israel closely monitors every threat posed by the Iranian terrorist regime and is prepared to confront it."
The White House did not respond to the newspaper's request for comment, but an American official said Trump would defend the United States and its allies against any potential threat.

articles.title_orig: US job postings jumped sharply in September, potentially a good sign for anyone seeking employment
articles.title_zh: US job postings jumped sharply in September, potentially a good sign for anyone seeking employment
articles.content_orig:
Job openings surged in September, as did the number of workers who quit their positions, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday, while hiring also rose and layoffs dropped.
In its monthly look at labor market slack and worker mobility, the BLS reported job openings at 7.52 million, up 333,000 from August and well above the Dow Jones consensus outlook for 7.15 million.
As a share of the total workforce, the rate of job openings increased to 4.5%, up 0.2 percentage point from the prior month, according to the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey . There are now some 414,000 more job openings than workers classified as unemployed, or about 1.05 openings to every available worker.
Openings rose in manufacturing (54,000) as well as state and local government (108,000) and professional and business services (106,000).
At the same time, the total of employees leaving their jobs spiked to 3.36 million, an increase of 321,000 from August and the highest level since March 2025. Quits are considered a barometer for worker confidence in finding new jobs after leaving their prior positions.
"There are more job openings than unemployed people in the United States right now. That doesn't solve all problems, but it's a big change from a year ago," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. "It's an encouraging sign that despite all the headwinds right now with high diesel and gas prices and ongoing inflation problems, companies are slowly increasing their hiring."
Hires rose on the month, up 131,000 to 5.4 million, while layoffs and discharges fell by 127,000 to 1.64 million, the lowest since March 2025.
The report comes ahead of the October nonfarm payrolls report, which the BLS will release Friday. The Wall Street consensus is for an increase of 59,000 after September eked out a gain of just 29,000, while the unemployment rate is figured to hold at 4.2%.
In other economic news Tuesday, September factory orders for manufactured goods jumped 1.8%, well above the estimate for 1.3% after increasing just 0.3% in August.

articles.title_zh: Moft’s new origami case adds a kickstand and grip to the iPhone Duo
articles.content_orig:
Published: 2nd November 2026
Sandmarc has launched its Pro Leather Case for the iPhone Duo, one of the first photography-focused cases for Apple’s new foldable.
Sandmarc is best known to mobile photographers for its add-on lenses and filters, and this case is built around that system. As well as protecting the phone, it has a mount for Sandmarc’s professional lenses, so you can add wide, telephoto or other optics in front of the Duo’s camera.
That’s particularly relevant on the Duo. Unlike the iPhone Pro models, it has no dedicated telephoto camera; it relies on a 2x crop from the 48MP main sensor. An optical add-on lens is one way to get more reach.
The case is made from full-grain leather, with a machined aluminium guard around the camera module. Wireless charging still works through it. Sandmarc has designed an open hinge so the case doesn’t restrict the fold, and the phone can still be propped at a range of angles. An optional front guard for the outer display is included.
Foldable cases are notoriously tricky. Apple’s own silicone case for the Duo has to be fixed in place with adhesive, so a case that leaves the hinge free and still adds a lens mount should appeal to anyone who wants to use the Duo as a serious camera.
We’d want to check how securely the lens mount locks in place and whether the case adds much bulk to an already chunky folded phone. We’ll report back if we get one to try.
The case is available now from Sandmarc. See the Sandmarc Pro Leather Case product page for pricing and colours, and Sandmarc’s announcement for more details.

articles.title_orig: Why the Anthropic IPO 'could be the swing vote' for Wall Street bank stocks
articles.title_zh: Why the Anthropic IPO 'could be the swing vote' for Wall Street bank stocks
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
After a rally through the first half of the summer, Wall Street bank stocks have lost their luster as rising interest rates threaten to cool their investment banking and trading booms that have powered their earnings.
Despite reporting sturdy third quarter results in early October, the signs of a slowdown in deals and trading activity have begun to pick up. The environment only raises the stakes for Anthropic's highly anticipated public debut , which could come as soon as Nov. 16 .
Each of the five biggest Wall Street banks has won a mandate to help in Anthropic's planned November listing, according to the startup's S-1 filing . On average, the IPO could represent a roughly 0.8% boost to banks' fourth quarter earnings, according to Evercore calculations, which are based on their fees earned from SpaceX's June IPO. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup stand to see the biggest lifts.
All in all, Anthropic's IPO "could be the swing vote" in 2026's final quarter for these banking giants, Evercore's Glenn Schorr wrote to clients on Tuesday.
So far in the fourth quarter, investors have already shown some selectivity in Wall Street bank stocks. From the beginning of October through Nov. 2, JPMorgan's ( JPM ) stock is up 3%, while Goldman Sachs' ( GS ) stock is flat and Morgan Stanley's ( MS ) stock is down 1.2%, according to Yahoo Finance data.  Shares of Citigroup ( C ) and Bank of America ( BAC ) are down 5% and 9%, respectively.
The KBW Nasdaq US bank index ( ^BKX ) is up more than 2% over the same period.
In October, worldwide investment banking activity fell 25% from a year earlier while US stock trading volumes tumbled 8%, according to Dealogic data cited by Evercore ISI.
A wider Federal Reserve survey released Monday found that US banks broadly tightened standards in the third quarter compared to the second quarter, reversing a four-quarter trend of easing standards amid fiercer competition. Borrowing demand also weakened across most loan categories.
What's adding even more uncertainty to the picture is Wall Street's growing skepticism of the AI investment boom, which has powered a wide swath of trading and dealmaking fees major banks have earned this year.
Anthropic's IPO comes as investors appear to be rethinking how much they are willing to pay for the world's biggest AI firms. Over recent days, investors have told Anthropic and its advisers the company's valuation should be around $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion, according to a Monday Wall Street Journal report . The valuation range is far below the $2 trillion mark reported earlier this year.
"Good companies come to market with good stories. There's plenty of capital to support those stories at reasonable valuations," Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said earlier Tuesday at the Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong.
Speaking alongside Solomon at the same event, Morgan Stanley CEO Ted Pick offered a similarly optimistic perspective on the AI investment boom.
"We're somewhere in the second inning of a nine-inning game," Pick said, referring to the enormous investments still expected in AI infrastructure.
Beyond Anthropic's IPO, bankers are also keeping a close eye on this week's midterm election results. Even a Democrat sweep would be unlikely to stop the Trump administration's deregulatory push, UBS bank analyst Erika Najarian said in a Monday note.
"We do think that there could be an acceleration of capital markets activity on the other side of results, especially if the market starts thinking of the possibility of a Democratic Presidential win in 2028, and thereby a tighter business environment for dealmaking," Najarian added.
